=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS === - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (step 6 line 29) | severity=high | confidence=5 flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash] PROBLEM: When an anchor prerequisite is unshipped and cannot join the bundle, line 42 says no bundle forms and the recommendation stays the single anchor plan. WHY: Step 6 requires the recommendation to be startable now, and the single-anchor hand-off omits the unshipped prerequisite, so the orchestrator starts a project that is not ready. Severity is MAJOR in the source reviewers' own terms (mapped to high). The anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 reviewer did not report this finding because it considered it a pre-existing property outside the diff. - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (output block lines 105-107) | severity=low | confidence=3 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash] PROBLEM: Line 42 requires an anchor prerequisite that joins as a member to be listed ahead of the anchor, but the output template hard-codes the anchor as the first bullet. WHY: An agent following the template literally prints the anchor first, which contradicts the dependency-order rule that implement-plan-ai.md relies on. Severity is NIT (mapped to low). z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised this only as a hardening suggestion. === END CONSENSUS FINDINGS === === CONSENSUS TASK GAPS === - requirement: PR DESCRIPTION: "A new output block lists the bundle with prerequisites first, cites how each plan is related, and prints one `Hand off:` command." expected_change_site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md lines 102-113 (the "When step 6 formed a bundle" output block) confidence=3 flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3] EVIDENCE: The block hard-codes the anchor as the first bullet and lists members after it. No clause tells the agent to reorder when a member is a prerequisite of the anchor. The prerequisites-first rule lives only in step 6 line 42. === END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS === === FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 === - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md; bundle output block line 106) | severity=NIT | confidence=3 PROBLEM: The last run lets an anchor prerequisite join as a member listed ahead of the anchor, but the output template still prints the anchor as the first bullet and does not say where an anchor prerequisite goes. WHY: An agent following the template literally lists the anchor before its prerequisite member, which contradicts the dependency-order rule implement-plan-ai.md relies on. The impact is cosmetic because the orchestrator adds the cross-plan DAG dependencies. - HARDENING: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py (`test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps`, `test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once`) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1 PROBLEM: The wording added during the review rounds has no test pin. This covers "**Prerequisites satisfied:**", "The anchor's own declared prerequisites follow the same rule", "drop repeats of the same resolved file", "name every bundled plan's repo-relative path in the project summary", and the two phase-counting phrases. WHY: A later edit could drop any of these phrases without failing a test. The suggested fix is one assert per phrase, about 6 lines. === END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 === === FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 === - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (step 6 line 29; lines 105-113) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5 PROBLEM: The fallback recommends the anchor as a single-plan dispatch even when one of its declared prerequisites is unshipped and cannot join the bundle. WHY: Step 6 requires the recommendation to be startable now. The dispatch names only the anchor, so the orchestrator launches a project that stalls on a prerequisite it does not know about. - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (output block lines 105-107) | severity=NIT | confidence=3 PROBLEM: Line 42 says an anchor prerequisite that joins must be "listed ahead of the anchor", but the output template hard-codes the anchor as the first bullet, with no tiebreaker. WHY: The agent would print the anchor first, while implement-plan-ai.md line 44 expects prerequisites first, so the two sides can disagree. - TASK_GAP: Requirement: PR DESCRIPTION: "A new output block lists the bundle with prerequisites first, cites how each plan is related, and prints one `Hand off:` command." | Expected change site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md lines 102-113 | severity=NIT | confidence=3 Evidence of absence: The block hard-codes the anchor first, and no clause reorders for an anchor-prerequisite member. - HARDENING: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py (`test_bundle_rule_lives_in_the_gate_after_the_pick` / `test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps`) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1 PROBLEM: The anchor-prerequisite behavior added in the last run is not pinned by any test assertion. WHY: The suggested fix is to add two asserts to step6, about 2 lines. === END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 === === FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna === - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (step 6 line 29) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5 PROBLEM: If an anchor has an unshipped prerequisite that cannot join the bundle, no bundle forms but the single anchor remains the recommendation. WHY: Step 6 requires the recommendation to be startable now, and the single-plan hand-off omits the unshipped prerequisite, so the orchestrator receives a project that is not ready. - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (output lines 105-107) | severity=NIT | confidence=3 PROBLEM: The rule requires an anchor prerequisite that joins to be listed ahead of the anchor, but the output template hard-codes the anchor first. WHY: Following the template produces a listing, including the copyable hand-off, that contradicts the required dependency order. - HARDENING: NONE | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=0 === END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna === === FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash === - .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md; hand-off line 112) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5 PROBLEM: When an anchor prerequisite is in-flight or screened out and not on the default branch, line 42 still recommends the single anchor plan, so the prerequisite gate applies only to bundle formation and is dropped on the fallback. WHY: The audit prints `Hand off: /implement-plan-claude docs/plans/P-plan.md`, naming only the anchor. The orchestrator project for P then starts while Q's work is unshipped, and P's phases build on code that does not exist yet. The fallback should instead exclude the anchor. - HARDENING: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md lines 104-113 vs line 42 | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1 PROBLEM: Line 42 requires an anchor prerequisite member to be listed ahead of the anchor, but the output block hard-codes the anchor as the first bullet. WHY: The suggested fix is to change line 106 to "- — anchor;

phases (list members that are the anchor's prerequisites ahead of it, in dependency order)" and to mirror the edit in the workflow-templates copy, about 2 lines. === END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
